races.name: Get Best Odds With Oddschecker Maiden Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Brosna Town
runners_data.note: Modest recent form (547-25), wears headgear, and trainer Jessica Bedi is 0/3 in the past 14 days; a genuine hold-up horse whose natural finishing position is further back than this map shows, which may limit its ability to land a telling blow.

runners_data.name: Credit Union
runners_data.note: Bedi's second runner, also a true closer, but three consecutive zeros in current form and a ⚠ fade flag in the finish make this very hard to recommend; 126 days off adds fitness doubt, and being denied its natural rearward slot only compounds the challenge.

runners_data.name: Eagle One
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old maiden hurdler returning after 200 days off, with no good-ground hurdle form on record from the last five runs; hold-up style suits a race with a real gallop, but the layoff and maiden status at this age are significant concerns.

runners_data.name: Ifyouhaveaplan
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Louise Allan, consistent if unspectacular (U-4256), and has run twice on good going without troubling the judge; 31 days since last run is fine, but needs a step forward in form to be competitive off OR 120.

runners_data.name: Jentobello
runners_data.note: Excellent record on similar going (5/6 sim-going, 2W5P) and has placed at 20f+ on multiple occasions, which makes this 2m4½f trip ideal; Iain Jardine sends runners to run well (6/35 in 14 days) and Richie McLernon is a significant booking — the profile fits this race shape very neatly.

runners_data.name: Just Keeps Rolling
runners_data.note: Three pulled-up efforts in latest form and wears a hood; Philip Kirby is 0/16 in the past 14 days and this horse's hold-up style on a modest record makes it hard to be enthusiastic at this stage.

runners_data.name: Way Maker
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and sole pace-setter in this race — James Bowen rides for his father Mickey and the horse has placed prominently (2W4P sim-going) so is no stranger to making the running at this trip; the key question is whether its OR 105 (lowest in the field) is enough quality to hold on.

runners_data.name: Arcimboldo
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with just one hurdle start (pulled up), returned 15 days ago; a natural hold-up horse whose finishing position in this field is compressed by the volume of closers, making it very difficult to assess what it might produce with so little evidence.

runners_data.name: Centurion's Sister
runners_data.note: Remarkably consistent without winning (0W5P sim-going), always placing on good ground, and Danny McMenamin is a solid booking; prominent style suits this race shape directly and the lighter weight (151lbs) is an asset — the profile says she should run well again, but the 0-from-multiple-chances form is a flag.

runners_data.name: Park Hall
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton takes a notable booking on a horse with a 112 record from just two hurdle starts, both on good ground; hold-up style (hg:h) means Park Hall is a genuine closer in a field where closers are squeezed, but class and jockey make this one to watch if it can find room late.

races.paceDynamic: Way Maker is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no rival likely to seriously contest that position, should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop throughout this 2m4½f maiden hurdle on good ground. The prominent types Jentobello, Ifyouhaveaplan, and Centurion's Sister will settle just behind, creating an organised field with a predictable pace shape rather than a pressured or falsely-run affair. Park Hall, Eagle One, and the three redistributed hold-up horses — Credit Union, Arcimboldo, and Brosna Town — will be housed further back, though their natural rear-of-field positioning is compressed by the volume of genuine hold-up types in this field, meaning their finishing kicks may be blunted by an inability to secure true backmarker slots. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can travel close to Way Maker's steady tempo, conserve energy through the middle section, and sustain their effort over the final two flights — horses like Jentobello and Centurion's Sister are archetypal beneficiaries of this controlled, front-runner-led shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Way Maker Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Way Maker establishes an uncontested lead and the pace remains measured, allowing prominent travellers to pounce late.
scenarios.body: Way Maker dictates on his own terms, setting a gallop that suits those just behind rather than stretching the field, and the race becomes a stamina test from the second-last where prominent types with a finishing effort prevail.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Surges Late
scenarios.trigger: If Way Maker's lead begins to collapse from three out, triggering a sustained challenge from the organised midfield chase pack.
scenarios.body: The race develops into a proper staying test as the gallop increases in the home straight, suiting a horse like Park Hall or Jentobello who can pick up efficiently from a handy position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply mid-race and catches the prominent runners flat, allowing a genuine finisher to come from off the pace.
scenarios.body: A horse racing with cover and timing a late run could benefit if the front group over-commits, though the redistributed hold-up types face the disadvantage of not having secured truly rearward positions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse and Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Way Maker stops suddenly or the race is run chaotically, turning the finish into a sprint-style scramble from two out.
scenarios.body: An erratic tempo would randomise the result and potentially drag the field into an even-paced finish where freshness and class edge — such as Park Hall's OR advantage — could be decisive.

watchPoints.text: Watch Way Maker's jumping closely from the outset — if he flukes an early error or is headed before halfway, the entire pace map collapses and the race becomes unpredictable for all promoted hold-up types.

Park Hall (Harry Skelton) is a hold-up horse in a field crowded with closers; watch whether Skelton opts to push forward rather than settle deep, as a tactical switch would change his scenario profile significantly.

Jentobello has been absent 298 days — watch the betting market move in the final hour, as any significant drift would suggest trainer Iain Jardine (6/35 14-day strike rate) is sending a ready horse but the market has reservations.

Credit Union and Brosna Town share the same trainer (Bedi) and both are displaced hold-up types — watch whether either is ridden more aggressively than expected, which would suggest stable orders have overridden natural style.

Centurion's Sister's consistent placing record (0W5P on sim-going) means she will likely hit the frame again, but watch whether she travels with more fluency than usual — any change in her jumping rhythm from the front could indicate a first win attempt.

races.name: Bet Smarter With Oddschecker+ Novices' Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Eternal Angel
runners_data.note: Six-year-old front-runner in good heart after back-to-back wins at 16f on Good, with Tom Lacey's stable slightly flat at 0/2 over 14 days but Jonathan Burke maintains a strong partnership; wears headgear (hg:h) and has an 8/11 record on similar going — has the form to match Loriko stride for stride.

runners_data.name: Loriko
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's five-year-old holds the highest OR (125) in the field and Harry Skelton is a formidable booking; two wins from front-running at 16f and 20f on Good give him versatility over this trip, and a 7/9 similar-going record underlines genuine course-condition suitability.

runners_data.name: Mayo
runners_data.note: Mickey Bowen's hold-up runner arrives on 70 days off which could mean freshness or ring-rustiness; James Bowen takes the ride and the horse has placed (3rd) once in four good-ground runs at this trip, but an OR of 120 with zero wins and no form above 7th recently makes him a passer rather than a winner without a front-runner implosion.

races.paceDynamic: Eternal Angel and Loriko are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over this 2m½f trip on Good ground at Market Rasen, creating a genuinely contested pace rather than a dawdle. Harry Skelton on Loriko (OR 125, the highest-rated runner) will be keen to dictate, but Tom Lacey's Eternal Angel has won twice from the front and Jonathan Burke won't simply surrender the rail — expect a proper battle for supremacy through the early hurdles. This honest, pressured gallop will strip out any false pace and place a premium on jumping cleanness and stamina through the final bend, as neither hold-up horse (Destination Unknown, Mayo) has the class or form to capitalise on a collapse up front. This race shape strongly favours whichever of the two front-runners can handle pressure and sustain their gallop most cleanly, with prominent-to-lead profiles the clear beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Strongest Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Loriko and Eternal Angel fight for the front and the better-class horse sustains the pace to the last hurdle cleanly.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners press each other at an honest gallop, burning off the hold-up horses whose lack of class makes a late challenge academic; whichever of Loriko or Eternal Angel jumps better in the home straight takes control.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Loriko Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Eternal Angel is unable to match Loriko's early stride and settles just off the pace, allowing Loriko to control fractions.
scenarios.body: Loriko sets a sustainable rhythm from the front under Harry Skelton, jumping slickly on good ground where he has a strong record (7/9 similar-going); without a genuine battle for the lead, he conserves energy and pulls clear from the last.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runners Tire, Hold-Up Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the pace battle between Loriko and Eternal Angel is fierce enough to cause both to weaken sharply approaching the final hurdle.
scenarios.body: Mayo, who has placed at this trip on good ground and arrives fresh off a 70-day break, would be best-placed to pick up the pieces, though his lack of wins and modest OR of 120 means he still needs things to go wrong for the leaders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Jumping Errors
scenarios.trigger: If jumping mistakes disrupt the front-runners mid-race and reshuffle positions dramatically.
scenarios.body: Market Rasen's tight track and a contested pace increase the chance of a novice error costing one of the leaders, but Destination Unknown's consistent tendency to fade in the finish and poor form string means even in chaos she is unlikely to capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Watch the battle between Loriko and Eternal Angel at the first two hurdles — whoever gains a clear lead early is likely to control the race, while a prolonged duel risks compromising both.
Eternal Angel's headgear (hood) and front-running style means any jumping hesitation under pressure from Loriko at a critical flight could cost Tom Lacey's runner momentum at a decisive moment.
Mayo's 70-day absence is the longest lay-off in the field — monitor early market moves to gauge whether stable confidence is genuine, as he has no winning form to lean on.

Destination Unknown's OR of 58 versus a field rated 120-125 represents an enormous class gulf; even in a race where the front-runners collapse, her established tendency to fade in the finish makes any involvement in a finish very unlikely.

Market Rasen's tight, undulating track rewards accurate jumping — with two novice front-runners pressing each other, watch for errors at the downhill hurdles on the far side where pace and unfamiliarity can combine.

races.name: Download The Oddschecker App Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: My Friend Sean
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong form at this trip and on good ground (9/15 sim-going strike rate), Jonathan Burke in the plate for Tom Lacey; tongue-tie and cheekpieces add focus, and 31 days since last run looks ideal — he is the textbook sit-and-pounce type who suits a contested early pace.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, My Friend Sean nevertheless shaped with plenty of promise when second last time out, and he returns after a 31-day break having run over today's trip and going before; our rating of 111 marks him as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Belle Le Grand
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton partners this hold-up mare for Dan Skelton in strong form; her lone win came over 17f on good and she stays honestly, but she needs things to go wrong up front — her best chance is if the two front-runners burn badly in the second mile.
runners_data.comment: Belle Le Grand won four starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with a 20-day turnaround leaving her fresh and race-ready; the risk is that her last three runs have all been out of the money.

runners_data.name: Dog Fox
runners_data.note: Prominent jumper who travels prominently and has solid course-type form over 16-17f on good ground (13/15 sim-going appearances); Jack Tudor keeps it simple on front-end horses and Dog Fox's jumping accuracy is the key — a clean round puts him right in the mix at the finish.
runners_data.comment: Dog Fox brings solid each-way credentials, finishing third two starts back and again five starts back, and has experience of today's trip and conditions; carrying 162 lb is the chief concern for a gelding yet to win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Ghasham
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with an eye-catching one-from-two win record over this sort of trip on good; Jonathan England rides quietly for Sam England and Ghasham's form figures of 2-2-1 in recent good-ground starts give him each-way claims if the pace creates enough of a target to run at.
runners_data.comment: Ghasham shaped well enough when third two starts back and won three starts back, giving him a mix of encouragement and slight frustration; he has experience over today's trip and going, but a hefty 161 lb is the key question mark here.

runners_data.name: Gower Prince
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner returning after 101 days off; has been placed twice on good ground and Jonjo O'Neill's yard is capable, but the layoff is a concern and sharing the lead with Genbu risks his stamina being tested earlier than connections would like — his chance depends on whether the other front-runner concedes.
runners_data.comment: Consistent front-runner who has finished second in each of his last two starts and has run over today's trip and going, suggesting conditions hold no fears; carrying a hefty 161 lb after 101 days off is the chief concern, and he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Clean Getaway
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's nine-year-old is a genuine deep hold-up horse at heart, boasting a 14/15 sim-going record and previous form figures of 1-3-3-4-5 at this sort of trip; racing off a compressed OR of 88 is attractive, but the redistribution note is honest — Joe Williamson is unlikely to find as much space at the back as this horse truly needs to produce his best.
runners_data.comment: Clean Getaway has managed just one win in his last five starts, with a fifth two runs back sandwiched between placed efforts, and ranked seventh of eight on our figures he faces a stiff task here; carrying 148 lb does not help, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Miss Denver
runners_data.note: Sam Twiston-Davies partners this six-year-old mare who is yet to win but has placed in four of her last five on good ground over comparable trips; she is a natural hold-up horse shuffled into a midfield mapping by the field dynamics, so she will not be producing a textbook late run — a consistent place-getter rather than a likely winner in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Miss Denver faces a stiff task at 146 lb, though she has run over today's trip and going before and her recent placed efforts suggest she remains competitive.

runners_data.name: Genbu
runners_data.note: Young four-year-old front-runner for Sarah-Jayne Davies with Charlie Price taking the ride; has won on good ground and shown enough early pace to press Gower Prince, but his chasing record is still developing (OR 85) and the step up to 2m1f with fences will test whether his jumping holds together under pressure.
runners_data.comment: Genbu has run over today's trip and going, and a rating of 91 suggests he holds more ability than his official mark of 85 implies; however, two fourth-place finishes in his last two starts are a concern, with the win coming five starts back.

races.paceDynamic: Gower Prince and Genbu are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off, creating a genuine, honest gallop over 2m1f on good ground — neither is likely to capitulate early, meaning this will not be a falsely-run race. That sustained pressure through the fences plays most naturally into the hands of prominent-to-midfield stalkers with proven good-ground stamina, horses who can track the pace without burning fuel early and then pick off the tiring leaders from the third-last. Clean Getaway and Miss Denver are both true hold-up types who have been mapped forward by redistribution because the rear of the field is overcrowded with similar profiles; in practice, neither is likely to secure their preferred ground-saving berth at the back, which blunts their chance in a shape that demands a late run from further back than they will actually be. The race shape decisively favours the prominent-tracking profile — a horse who sits just off the two leaders, travels within itself, and produces a clean jumping round to collar the front pair before the last.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Stalkers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Gower Prince and Genbu burn each other off at an honest clip, leaving a prominent tracker to cruise into contention from the third-last.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners press each other throughout, ensuring enough pace to expose any faders, while the horses who sit a length or two off the lead in a rhythm preserve enough to power home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Gower Prince or Genbu asserts early enough to dictate solo, setting a controlled but untested gallop and jumping away cleanly.
scenarios.body: One of the duo gets a soft lead after the other capitulates or makes jumping errors, allowing the front-runner to control tempo and steal a decisive advantage from the fourth fence.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final circuit and a big gap opens up for late-closers to exploit from the home straight.
scenarios.body: Belle Le Grand, a genuine hold-up horse with strong good-ground form and Harry Skelton aboard, would be the primary beneficiary if the tempo unexpectedly flattens and runners come back to her.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Blanket Finish, Field Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or fatigue disrupt all the pace-setters and the race dissolves into a scramble from the second-last.
scenarios.body: A messy, attritional finish suits the horse who stays on most doggedly regardless of position, with the lower-weighted runners who handle the rough-and-tumble potentially benefiting from the chaos.

watchPoints.text: Gower Prince and Genbu will clash for the lead from the first fence — watch which of the two blinks first, because if one capitulates and concedes the front, the race dynamic shifts immediately from contested to controlled.

My Friend Sean's headgear (cheekpieces and tongue-tie) suggests a horse that has needed assistance to fully apply himself — if he fails to travel smoothly behind the leaders in the early stages, his prominent position becomes a liability rather than an asset.

Dog Fox produced a 'V' in his most recent form and has a 'P' in his string — jumping safety in this 2m1f chase is non-negotiable, and a single fence error at a crucial stage could cost him any chance he has when the race quickens at the third-last.

Clean Getaway's redistribution is the key context flag — Joe Williamson is an inexperienced conditional and if he cannot engineer the wide, late run his horse truly needs, the OR 88 advantage is wasted; watch whether he can find daylight from the home turn.

Belle Le Grand arrives on a 20-day turnaround with Harry Skelton booking suggesting connections see fitness; monitor her jumping at the early fences as her record over course-and-distance includes a win here at 17f — if she settles cleanly she is the most dangerous outsider if the front pair tire.

races.name: Oddschecker Free Bets Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Ernest Gray
runners_data.note: Proven course-and-distance profile at this sort of Good-ground trip with a win and place from five similar-going runs; Jonathan Burke rides for the in-form Alan King yard (1/14 past fortnight), and the prominent style is ideal for a race where pace is controlled — hood retained.|
runners_data.comment: Ernest Gray won four starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with his rating of 125 suggesting he holds strong claims here; the concern is that he has finished fourth or further in his last three starts.

runners_data.name: Ballintubber Boy
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here, Sam Twiston-Davies takes the ride for his own family yard; exceptional Good-ground record (13/15 with two wins, eight places) makes him a formidable lead horse at 2m7f, and the tongue tie is worth noting as a breathing aid over this extended trip.|
runners_data.comment: Ballintubber Boy was third last time out, and a second four starts back underlines his consistency, though he remains yet to win in his last five starts; experience over today's trip and going, combined with a rating of 126, makes him the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Kiwi de Cotte
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton sends out this six-year-old with Harry Skelton in the saddle, a powerful combination; placed at three from three on similar going, won over 2m3f and steps up to 2m7f here which is an open question, but if the stamina holds he is prominently placed to take full advantage of a controlled tempo.|
runners_data.comment: Kiwi de Cotte has pulled up twice in his last five starts, making him hard to trust despite wins in the same span; he has run over today's trip and going, but ranked fifth of six on our figures, he faces a stiff task under 159 lb.

runners_data.name: Belvedere Blast
runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley's eight-year-old arrives on the back of two Good-ground places at 2m4f and is a hold-up horse by trade; the 5lb claim of Oakley Brown is a mild positive on weight but this runner needs the pace to be honest to fire from off it, and there is no certainty of that here.|
runners_data.comment: Belvedere Blast has back-to-back thirds in recent starts and returns here 28 days on, with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour; the chief concern is that ninth last time out and a record of 0 wins in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Lowlands
runners_data.note: Danny McMenamin partners this Nicky Richards-trained seven-year-old who won over 2m4f on Good ground last season and has a decent placed record at the trip; a natural hold-up type whose finishing effort is dependent on a true pace developing, and with Ballintubber Boy likely to set a controlled tempo, getting into the race from the rear may come too late.|
runners_data.comment: Lowlands shaped with real promise when runner-up two starts back and built on that with a win three starts back, suggesting she retains her form well; she has experience of today's distance and going, though a fourth last time out raises a mild question mark.

runners_data.name: Parikarma
runners_data.note: Samuel Drinkwater's nine-year-old carries the lowest OR in the field (97) and is a genuine hold-up horse by history; with multiple confirmed hold-up types in this field, she is expected to race closer than her natural style dictates — racing out of role tempers her chance, and the 7lb claim of Miss Imogen Mathias helps on weight but not positioning.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Parikarma faces a stiff task at 145 lb, though she has run over today's trip and going before and showed placed form three starts back and last time out.

races.paceDynamic: Ballintubber Boy is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a six-runner field, he is highly likely to dictate from the outset at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 2m7f trip on Good ground. Ernest Gray and Kiwi de Cotte will push to track him prominently, creating a compressed early order with no pressure from behind to force an overly-generous tempo. The hold-up trio of Belvedere Blast, Lowlands, and Parikarma will be last away, though the field holds more confirmed hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate in that position — Parikarma in particular, mapped to midfield, is unlikely to secure a true rear-of-field pitch and may need to be placed closer than ideal. This shape — a lone leader setting a measured pace with prominent trackers well-placed — strongly favours horses racing prominently or just off the pace, who can travel sweetly and produce their effort without having to find an extra gear from a cold position late on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ballintubber Boy Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Ballintubber Boy dictates an uncontested, honest gallop and his prominent pursuers lack the finishing kick to peg him back.
scenarios.body: Ballintubber Boy has strong Good-ground form credentials (13/15 on similar going) and, allowed to roll along at his own tempo unchallenged, can eke out enough of a gap at each hurdle to hold on; Ernest Gray and Kiwi de Cotte, tracking close throughout, are best placed to be first to ask questions but must quicken on a flattening track.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Ballintubber Boy's lead is reeled in from the home turn by one of the prominent trackers who has conserved energy through a controlled mid-race tempo.
scenarios.body: Kiwi de Cotte, freshened over this longer 2m7f trip having placed at 2m3f, or Ernest Gray — a course-proven winner on similar ground — could have enough in reserve to sweep past as Ballintubber Boy tires on the run-in; this is the most natural second shape given how compressed and prominent-heavy the field is.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Gets Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest early and the prominent horses burn each other out, creating a gap for a held-up finisher.
scenarios.body: Lowlands has a healthy record at this sort of trip and won over 2m4f on Good ground before, so if the front end cuts themselves up she has the form to finish powerfully; Belvedere Blast has placed twice recently on Good going at marathon trips but is likely to need a truly strong pace to get involved.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Disrupts Shape
scenarios.trigger: If early interference, a jumping error from Ballintubber Boy, or an unexpected injection of pace scrambles the established order.
scenarios.body: Parikarma, racing out of her natural hold-up role and expected to be closer than comfortable, could get competitive if chaos promotes her to a position that suits; however, given her OR of 97 and a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.92 indicating she is operating out of role, this outcome is the least likely and depends on extraneous factors rather than form.

watchPoints.text: Ballintubber Boy's jumping under Sam Twiston-Davies is the single biggest swing factor — a clean round and uncontested lead makes him very hard to catch over 2m7f on Good ground, but any error at a hurdle could end his advantage instantly.

Kiwi de Cotte's stamina over 2m7f is unproven — he has only run to 2m3f previously, and Harry Skelton may need to be patient, risking a late finish in a race where prominent horses are likely to be rewarded.

Parikarma's redistribution to a midfield role means she is not racing at her natural position; watch whether Miss Imogen Mathias (7lb claimer) can settle her effectively against her instincts, as a poorly-judged ride could compromise what little chance she has at OR 97.

Ernest Gray has run six times on Good or similar going, placing in seven of fifteen such efforts across his career — his consistency in this going band is a notable positive, but the 39-day absence after a fourth-place finish is worth monitoring for race sharpness.

Lowlands and Belvedere Blast are both hold-up types in a race where only one horse is setting a genuinely controlled pace — if neither can get the strong gallop they need to close, both may find themselves flattening out without having found their race.

races.name: Oddschecker+ Subscription Service Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: The Clonmel Kid
runners_data.note: Won at 2m4f on Good 39 days ago under Philip Kirby, who has a solid record at the track; races from hold-up, but with a contested front-running pace he should get a good tow into contention, and his sim-going record (1W4P on Good) gives confidence in conditions.

runners_data.name: A Dublin Job
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will press for the lead from the off; Cameron Johnstone-Baker (7lb claim) is a booking to note for connections, visor worn, and the horse has a reasonable Good-ground record (3W4P in 15 similar-going runs) though has shown little in recent outings.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, A Dublin Job has nonetheless been running to a fair level, and with experience of today's trip and going, the step up in quality suggested by our rating of 111 makes him the one to beat despite carrying 165 lb.

runners_data.name: Ribeye
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old hold-up horse with Danny McMenamin in the saddle; best form comes on Good ground (1W6P), the step back to 2m5½f may help after a run over 3m, but a run of non-completions and poor finishes makes reliability a concern.
runners_data.comment: Ribeye has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 105 suggests he holds strong claims here as the third-ranked runner in the field; yet to score in his last five starts and a pulled-up effort two runs back remain the chief concerns.

runners_data.name: Huckleberry Sting
runners_data.note: Strong recent form (2W5P on Good, last five all placed or won at 2-3m) and the most naturally talented closer in this field; however, in a race with two front-runners dominating, his instinct to settle at the rear means he may find himself racing closer than ideal, tempering his expected finishing kick.
runners_data.comment: Huckleberry Sting won two starts back and was second last time out, showing he retains ability, though he is ranked sixth of eight on our rating and a 160 lb burden is a stiff ask as he steps back in grade.

runners_data.name: La Quarite
runners_data.note: 340 days off the track is the outstanding query — James Bowen takes the ride for father Mickey Bowen, and the yard has a quiet recent strike rate (0/2 in 14 days); on Good ground she has shown tactical speed and won at 2m5f before, but fitness after such a lay-off is a real concern.
runners_data.comment: La Quarite landed a win earlier in this sequence and was runner-up last time out, showing he retains ability, and he has experience of today's trip and going; the sole concern is a lengthy 340-day absence.

runners_data.name: Huit Reflets
runners_data.note: Naturally prominent, Jamie Hamilton booked, and trainer Mark Walford has a reasonable 14-day return (1/9); best form has come at shorter trips (2m1f), so the 2m5½f trip is a question mark, but he gets a good racing position in the likely pace scenario and won't be far away early.
runners_data.comment: Huit Reflets arrives here on the back of a runner-up finish last time out, yet remains winless in his last five starts, and a ninth three starts back is a blot on an otherwise consistent profile; distance and going experience help, though 154 lb is no gimme.

runners_data.name: Uncle Al
runners_data.note: Back from 22 days off, Conor O'Farrell continues; has won at 3m on Good and shown up-and-down form (2-UP16), but is a genuine closer who is likely to be forced closer to the pace than natural in this shape, which blunts his best weapon — the ability to produce a fresh late effort.
runners_data.comment: Uncle Al's chequered recent profile — pulling up and unseating in his last five starts alongside that sole win — makes him difficult to fancy, and he is ranked last but one on our figures; has run over today's trip and going, and 22 days since his reappearance leaves him at least fit.

runners_data.name: Fast Deal
runners_data.note: Bottom weight at OR=64 with a form string of FP-866 suggesting limited current ability; James Best takes the ride and the horse is a true hold-up type who will be squeezed towards the pace by the front-running tempo — with no wins or places on similar going in his last five, the numbers don't encourage.
runners_data.comment: Fast Deal has tumbled to a mark of 64 off a sequence that reads fell, pulled up, eighth, then consecutive sixths, and our figures rank him last of eight here — hard to make a case for him despite the experience over today's trip and going.

races.paceDynamic: A Dublin Job and La Quarite are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over 2m5½f on Good ground at Market Rasen, creating a genuine, honest gallop that is unlikely to collapse at any stage. The duel between them should set a rhythm that stretches the field and leaves little room for late reserves, favouring horses that can travel smoothly in the slipstream rather than those forced to make up ground from a cold. The field carries more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Huckleberry Sting, Uncle Al, and Fast Deal are all genuine closers who are likely to find themselves racing closer to the pace than ideal, compromising their chance of delivering a true late run. This race shape — a contested, honest-paced chase over a stiff 2m5½f — firmly favours prominent racers and relaxed stalkers who can sit just off a strong gallop and travel into contention, rather than true hold-up horses who need a truly slowly-run race to unleash a late challenge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If A Dublin Job and La Quarite fight it out up front and the honest gallop stretches the field, leaving a prominent or mid-pack stalker to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners take the sting out of each other over the final mile, and a horse travelling smoothly just off the pace arrives with a well-timed run to collar them approaching the last. Ribeye and The Clonmel Kid, both hold-up horses with strong Good-ground profiles, are ideally placed to exploit this shape if they can get close enough to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If La Quarite or A Dublin Job shakes off the rival pace-setter mid-race and is allowed to stride clear on their own terms.
scenarios.body: One of the two leaders outguns the other early on the final circuit, finds a rhythm, and the honest gallop becomes a controlled one under a dominant front-runner. La Quarite, returning after a 340-day absence but proven on Good ground and handled by a sharp yard, would be the likeliest individual to stamp authority if fresh enough to sustain the effort.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Fail To Fire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to compress the field and none of the redistibuted hold-up types can get to their natural position, the winner comes from the prominent pack.
scenarios.body: Huckleberry Sting, Uncle Al, and Fast Deal — all genuine closers — are forced to race closer to the pace than suits them, burning their finishing kick too early and failing to land a blow. Huit Reflets, who sits naturally prominent, benefits from the compressed field and the strong gallop doing the donkey work ahead.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Burn, Late Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners set a false or erratic pace and the hold-up horses manage to secure their natural position off the back of the field.
scenarios.body: A Dublin Job or La Quarite makes an early mistake or eases back, causing the tempo to drop in the middle stages and giving the true closers a genuine late-race target. Huckleberry Sting, with a 2W5P record on similar going and strong recent form, is the most dangerous beneficiary if this unlikely shape develops, though the structural odds of it materialising in a two-runner-led race are low.

watchPoints.text: A Dublin Job and La Quarite — watch whether either blinks in the opening mile; if one folds early, the other could steal a march that the rest cannot close.
La Quarite's fitness after 340 days off is the single biggest unknown — if she blows up from the third-last, she could badly interfere with horses trying to travel behind her.

Huckleberry Sting, Uncle Al, and Fast Deal — monitor their positions at the first fence; if all three are pushed forward by the tempo, the expected late-race challenge from the hold-up group evaporates entirely.

Huit Reflets is the only confirmed prominent type outside the two leaders — watch whether Hamilton uses the early pace to slot into third or fourth, as that position could be pivotal if the duelling front-runners tire late.

The Clonmel Kid's jockey Joe Williamson — note how quickly he commits after the last fence; the horse has a win from hold-up on this trip and could be the value stalker if the pace is genuinely honest throughout.

races.name: oddschecker.com Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: No More Bolero
runners_data.note: Won his last two starts over this sort of distance on good ground and carries the visor; holds the clearest tactical advantage as the race's lone front-runner, though any dramatic step up in class or pace pressure would expose him.
runners_data.comment: No More Bolero arrives in fine fettle, winning two on the bounce and scoring three times in his last five starts, and he has experience of both today's trip and going; the chief concern is a hefty 168 lb to shoulder.

runners_data.name: God Of Fire
runners_data.note: Ran out a winner over 2m4f on good ground last time and has a live profile tracking from a prominent position; Jonjo O'Neill yard firing at only 0/2 in the 14-day window is minor caution, but the form profile is strong.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving God Of Fire a strong hand here; carrying 164 lb is the one query, but he is the top-rated runner in this field and arrives in good heart off a 33-day break.

runners_data.name: Four Decades
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has failed to land a blow in recent starts over similar distances on good ground; the sim-going record (0W0P) and consistent back-of-field finishes make it hard to construct a winning scenario.
runners_data.comment: Four Decades has run over today's going and returns on a sharp 22-day turnaround, with our rating of 99 marking her out as a leading threat in a competitive field; the concern is that she has been winless in her last five starts, with a best recent finish of fourth.

runners_data.name: Fine Point
runners_data.note: Won over 2m on good ground and ran well over 2m2f at the same track type; wears hood (headgear), has a solid sim-going record (2W5P), and the 70-day break is the only query around a horse who otherwise fits this race's shape very well.
runners_data.comment: Fine Point won two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, giving him relevant experience, but third last time out and a 70-day absence are the counterweights; at 161 lb, the weight ask is also far from straightforward for a mid-field proposition.

runners_data.name: Lone Star
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who trades on consistency rather than a win; has a strong sim-going record (1W4P, 13 runs) and runs tongue-tied, usually prominent — a reliable pace companion for the winner but unlikely to have enough to overhaul fresher rivals late.
runners_data.comment: Lone Star arrives here after a third last time out, and a third five starts back frames a consistent profile that our rating of 100 suggests is handily treated; she has run over today's trip and going, and at 158 lb the weight burden is the one factor to overcome.

runners_data.name: Ashdown Forest
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 2m on good ground and Harry Skelton takes over; genuine hold-up operator whose best chance arrives if the pace is strong enough to string out the field, but a slow-run race on a flat track could leave him with too much to do.
runners_data.comment: Beaten in four of his last five starts and ranked seventh of ten on our figures, Ashdown Forest faces a stiff ask under 156 lb, though he does arrive on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's going.

runners_data.name: Ballynoe Boy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with decent form over 2m4f-2m6f; the step back to 2m2½f is a slight query, and the sim-going record in softer conditions (0W2P) is better than on good — not obviously well placed.
runners_data.comment: Ballynoe Boy has shown he can mix it in this grade with a third three starts back, though winless in his last five and returning after 48 days off, the 153 lb burden may test his resolve on this occasion.

runners_data.name: Quick Of The Night
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with a decent sim-going strike rate (2W7P) who wants to race prominently but faces a field where that berth is already taken; running out of role will blunt his chance and recent form (0 from last five) backs that concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Quick Of The Night makes a tough case despite the experience over today's trip and going; that unplaced effort last time out, off 146 lb, does little to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Red Trail
runners_data.note: Wears tongue-tie and is a genuine hold-up type who finds himself mapped centrally here; a string of modest finishes, a pulled-up run last time, and a sim-going record of 0W1P from nine runs make it very difficult to see a route to victory.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time and winless in her last five starts, Red Trail is hard to fancy at the foot of our rankings, though she has experience of today's going and a 57-day break may have helped her freshness.

runners_data.name: Papillondelumiere
runners_data.note: Visor-wearing prominent racer who has pulled up twice in recent starts and whose sim-going figures on good ground are limited (0W0P from four); the redistribution to midfield reflects a crowded front end and combines with stale form to significantly undermine its prospects.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and yet to score, Papillondelumiere has shown little in recent starts — back-to-back pulls-up following a sixth and seventh — but lightly raced and open to better, he could strip fitter here just 20 days on from his latest outing.

races.paceDynamic: No More Bolero is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the early lead, should settle into a comfortable, uncontested gallop around Market Rasen's flat, right-handed circuit over 2m2½f on good ground. God Of Fire and Fine Point are the natural prominent types best placed to track him from positions two to four, with Lone Star also likely to race in the first half of the field. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred ground — Quick Of The Night and Papillondelumiere are genuine prominent racers who will likely find themselves shuffled back into midfield as the early positions fill, while Red Trail, a true hold-up horse, is similarly displaced toward the centre of the pack on the map. With No More Bolero dictating a sustainable, honest but unspectacular gallop, this race shape favours prominent racers who can travel just off the pace and pounce approaching the last — horses like God Of Fire and Fine Point who can use No More Bolero's consistent tempo without being dragged into a war.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Holds, Front Rules
scenarios.trigger: If No More Bolero controls from the front and the pace remains honest but never brutal, allowing front-rank horses to conserve energy.
scenarios.body: No More Bolero's uncontested lead on good ground over a track he handles well (4W in sim-going) means he can dictate tempo and keep enough in reserve; prominent horses immediately behind him inherit the race's energy profile perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If No More Bolero sets a mildly generous pace and a prominent tracker produces a well-timed move between the last two flights.
scenarios.body: Fine Point (won at this trip on good ground, good sim-going record) or God Of Fire (recent course winner) hit the front as No More Bolero ties up, rewarding those who raced within striking distance throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply in the back straight and the mid-to-rear runners benefit from a strung-out field and a strong gallop.
scenarios.body: Ashdown Forest (recent winner, Harry Skelton, handles good ground at this trip) is the most credible late finisher as a genuine hold-up type; Ballynoe Boy also has claims if the race is truly run at a demanding tempo.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If No More Bolero sets an unsustainably slow crawl and the race turns into a sprint from the home turn.
scenarios.body: This scenario benefits any horse with a sharp turn of foot on good ground but is inherently unpredictable; Ashdown Forest and Fine Point both have relatively strong speed figures and could thrive in a falsely-run race.

watchPoints.text: No More Bolero has won his last two and controls the pace completely — if he gets an uncontested lead and sets a manageable gallop, the race may effectively be decided turning for home.

Quick Of The Night and Papillondelumiere are natural front-runners who will be squeezed for early position — watch for a congested first half-mile that could unsettle either runner and disrupt their rhythm.
Fine Point has not run for 70 days and wears headgear; if she shows any signs of ring-rustiness in the early stages, her prominent position could become a liability rather than an asset.

Ashdown Forest is the most interesting hold-up horse in the field — Harry Skelton's booking and a recent win suggest connections believe there is more to come, but she needs a genuine gallop to deliver her challenge from off the pace.

Market Rasen's flat, galloping track on good ground typically rewards horses that travel prominently and jump fluently — monitor jumping errors, particularly from the hold-up horses who will be doing their racing in traffic early on.
